description: manifest.json at the root of an activation-capture directory, beside examples.jsonl and shard_NNNNN.npz

notes.dtype: float32 is the only value both writers emit. The shard holds activations of a bf16 model, and widening bf16 to float32 is exact, so the stored values are the model's own. float16 is not a safe alternative: it carries 5 exponent bits to bf16's 8, so residual-stream outliers that bf16 represents saturate to inf. bfloat16 on disk is not available at all - numpy has no bfloat16 dtype and .npy has no descriptor for it. Both writers emitted float16 before this contract constrained the field, and those captures remain readable (no reader inspects dtype) but are not numerically comparable to float32 ones; captures are a regenerable cache, so re-run rather than migrate. schema_version is deliberately not bumped: no required field changed, and bumping would invalidate every existing capture at load_manifest.
notes.site: Which point of each layer the rows were taken at, as the Rust tap seam's own name for it ('layer_output' - the decoder block's complete output, after the post-MLP residual add and the layer output scale). 'layers' alone names half of where an activation came from; the other half was recoverable only because both writers happen to capture the same point, which is a property of this moment rather than of the format. Emitted by the Rust writer only, on the capture_backend precedent: the Python writer predates it and no reader requires it, so teaching interp/probes/capture.py to emit it is a behavior change belonging to its own commit. The shard keys stay layer_<L> and schema_version is deliberately not bumped - one site means the key is unambiguous, and changing it would break interp/probes/capture.py load_capture for no information gain. A second site is what makes the key ambiguous: at that point the key grows a site suffix and schema_version bumps, and this field stops being writer-only.
notes.capture_backend: Emitted by the Rust writer only. The Python writer predates it and no reader requires it, so it is writer-only rather than required. Adding it to the Python writer is a behavior change that belongs in its own commit.
notes.dataset_sha256: Not comparable across writers. Rust hashes the file's raw bytes (std::fs::read); Python hashes text-mode f.read(), which normalizes CRLF to LF. The two digests agree for an LF-only dataset and differ for a CRLF one. Both are internally consistent; neither is wrong. Do not 'fix' one side to match the other without deciding which domain the field means and bumping schema_version - a test pins the divergence so a one-sided change fails.
notes.tokenizer_fingerprint: Not comparable across writers, and documented as such at activation-capture.rs:287-291. Python hashes name_or_path, len(tokenizer), and the chat template; Rust hashes the model file path, the vocabulary length, and an empty template, because a raw-text capture applies no template. Each keeps its own artifacts internally consistent from capture through train to score.
notes.envelope: The required set is a superset of the shared report envelope in common/reports.py: schema_version, exactly one discriminator (artifact), a stamp (created), and git_sha. Both writers satisfy validate_report today, though that module scopes itself to reports rather than artifact manifests.
